title: D5 benchmark instrument: host-real fixture generator + spawn-inclusive p95 runner
action: Build the D5 acceptance instrument in the crate named exactly `queen-bench` (member already scaffolded by rust-port-1 — do not touch crates/Cargo.toml): (a) fixture generator subcommand producing a host-real .bee store at pinned minimum sizes (decisions.jsonl min 700KB, reservations min 600KB, backlog.jsonl min 250KB, min 250 cell files) — generator REFUSES smaller sizes; (b) bench runner measuring spawn-inclusive wall-time p95 over min 50 runs per command. Budget is a flag: --budget-ms, default 5 (dev gate per D5); CI perf smoke will pass --budget-ms 15 (same command, no second tool). The bench resolves the queen-bee binary from the workspace target dir (crates/target/release/queen-bee), overridable via --bin-path. `--self-test` asserts BOTH directions (advisor note 2): all four sub-pinned-size refusal cases refuse, AND one happy-path generation succeeds, measurably meets every pin, and passes a `node .bee/bin/bee.mjs status --json` sanity read against the generated store (bee.mjs invoked with cwd at the generated root; store must include .bee/onboarding.json so root resolution stays inside it). `--check` runs the p95 floor gate on `queen-bee ping`. Slice-0 scope: prove the floor and record the node baseline (`node -e ""`) in the JSON report. Spike evidence: .bee/spikes/rust-port/coldexec measured p95 2.63ms over 100 runs on this WSL2 box (floor exists, 47% headroom).

truths: --check exits non-zero if no-op p95 is at or above the budget (default 5ms)
--self-test exits non-zero unless all four sub-pinned-size refusal cases refuse AND a happy-path generation meets every pin AND the generated store passes a bee.mjs status --json sanity read
JSON report includes node baseline alongside queen-bee percentiles

artifacts.substantive: fixture generator + p95 runner in one crate, no stubs; JSON report emitted

key_links: bench spawns the release queen-bee binary built in the same verify invocation (workspace build precedes the run)
generated fixture is the input contract for bee-parity (rust-port-4)
prohibitions: Never benchmark against a fixture smaller than the D5 pinned sizes
timings.jsonl is not used as acceptance data (per D5)
No edits to crates/Cargo.toml (members final per rust-port-1)
Sanity-read subprocess never runs with cwd inside the repo tree

verify: cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml && cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p queen-bench -- --self-test && cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p queen-bench -- --check

trace.outcome: queen-bench builds a D5 host-real fixture generator (--generate, refuses any of the four pinned sizes below floor: decisions.jsonl>=700KB, reservations.json>=600KB, backlog.jsonl>=250KB, cells>=250) and a spawn-inclusive p95 runner. --self-test proves both directions: all 4 sub-pinned-size refusal cases refuse, and a happy-path generation measurably meets every pin plus passes a real node .bee/bin/bee.mjs status --json sanity read against the generated store (temp-dir root, never cwd inside the repo tree). --check gates queen-bee ping spawn-inclusive p95 over 50 runs against --budget-ms (default 5, CI passes 15), exits non-zero at/above budget, and always prints a JSON report with queen-bee percentiles alongside the node -e "" baseline. Binary resolved from the workspace target dir (sibling of queen-bench's own exe), overridable via --bin-path. Measured this run: queen-bee ping p95 ~1.1-1.8ms (47%+ headroom under 5ms), node baseline p95 ~25-28ms.
